metadata.name: Thomas Hobbes
metadata.description: English philosopher who argued that an undivided sovereign is necessary to protect people from civil conflict.
metadata.scope: Documented writings and public positions in 1640–1679. Modern scenarios are explicitly counterfactual inferences from those positions, not claims that the subject answered this quiz. Conditional answers retain competing principles. Assessment research accessed 4 October 2026.

axes.brief: A sovereign person or assembly needs final, undivided authority to secure peace. Consent establishes sovereignty but does not require repeated competitive elections or ongoing accountability to a rival power.
axes.counterEvidence: Sovereignty may be democratic, aristocratic or monarchical. Answers reject compulsory democratic procedures, not the logical possibility of a sovereign assembly; military usurpation is not a routine right.

Hobbes permits sovereignty in a person or assembly and values capable counsel, but expertise alone neither confers sovereignty nor obliges an electorate to select it. Expert selection and popular authorisation can each be legitimate if they establish a durable sovereign; neither is the required method.

review.notes: Independent evidence audit by a different agent from the assessment author. Checked every answer against all 240 exact bank questions, agreement directions, stated period and retained source context, with targeted rereads of primary texts. Repaired systematic rationale reversals in universal voting, offensive criticism and graduation-alone residence; removed repeated generic closing boilerplate. Qualified executive authority by whether the sovereign is a monarch or assembly; distinguished work duties from fixed benefit expiry. Corrected materialism-versus-heredity errors using Leviathan VIII and made ownership alternatives concrete. Numeric changes: democracy-autocracy-04: 2 -> 1; high-redistribution-low-redistribution-08: 1 -> 0; culture-nature-02: 0 -> -1; culture-nature-04: 1 -> 0; culture-nature-10: 0 -> -1; culture-nature-12: 1 -> 0. Limitations: contemporary visas, clinical AI, brain implants, embryo enhancement and trait-level causal comparisons remain explicitly counterfactual educated inferences, not reported opinions. Neutral answers were reviewed as competing principles or permissible institutional arrangements; sparse Culture/Nature evidence remains low-confidence and is not a scientific claim. No scores or similarity thresholds were targeted. Validation and batch-neighbour review are separate from source accuracy; parent retains archive and publication responsibility. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
